configuration.title: AMXX Pawn All-In
config.fileExtensions.description: Source file suffixes that should automatically activate the AMXX Pawn language. By default this is only `.sma`. Put include suffixes in Include File Extensions instead.
config.includeFileExtensions.description: Extra include file suffixes that should automatically activate AMXX Pawn and can be resolved by Pawn #include directives when the include name has no explicit extension. The compiler-style include suffixes `.inc`, `.p`, `.i`, and `.pawn` are always enabled and cannot be removed here.
config.detectPawnLanguageByIncludes.mark: Automatically switch an opened non-AMXX Pawn document to AMXX Pawn when it contains a resolved Pawn include and Pawn-specific syntax. Documentation and common C/C++ files are ignored.
config.projectLocalIncludePaths.descript: Project-local include sources to search first. Each item can be a folder name, a relative path, an absolute path, or a specific include file. Relative paths resolve from the workspace root, or from the current file folder when no workspace is open.
config.globalIncludePaths.description: Global fallback include sources. Each item can be a folder or a specific include file, using either relative or absolute paths. Relative paths resolve from workspace roots, or from the current file folder when no workspace is open. Used only after project-local include sources.
config.globalCompilerPath.markdownDescri:
Global fallback path to the AMXX compiler executable `amxxpc.exe`, or to a folder that contains `amxxpc.exe`. This is used only after checking project-local compiler locations first, and then the current file folder if no project compiler was found.

To add a compile hotkey in VS Code, open Keyboard Shortcuts and bind the command `amxxPawnAllIn.compileCurrentFile` with the condition `editorTextFocus && editorLangId == amxxpawn`.
config.compilerOutputDirectory.markdownD: Directory for compiled `.amxx` output. If empty, the result is written next to the current source file. Absolute paths are used as-is. Relative paths are resolved using Compiler Output Directory Base. Missing folders are created automatically.
config.compilerOutputDirectoryBase.markd: Control which folder should be used as the base when Compiler Output Directory is a relative path. The recommended default writes into the project root when the current file belongs to a workspace folder, and falls back to the current source file folder otherwise.
Recommended default. Resolve relative output directories from the current file's project root when the file belongs to a workspace folder. If there is no project root, fall back to the source file folder.
Resolve relative output directories from the current source file folder. This preserves the old behavior where compiling a file in a subfolder creates or uses `compiled` inside that subfolder.
Resolve relative output directories from the folder that contains the resolved compiler executable when available. If no compiler path is resolved yet, fall back to the source file folder.
config.compilerOptions.description: Additional command-line options passed to amxxpc.exe. Each entry should be a single raw compiler argument. Output file handling from Compiler Output Directory is still applied automatically.
config.compileRevealTarget.markdownDescr: Control which issue should receive editor focus automatically after compilation finishes. This affects navigation only and is independent from when the compiler output channel itself is revealed. The recommended `all-issues-priority` mode jumps to the first live validation error when available, otherwise to the first compiler error, and then to the first compiler warning.
config.compileRevealTarget.enum.never: Never jump to an issue automatically after compile. Use this if you want compilation to finish quietly and handle navigation yourself.
config.compileRevealTarget.enum.live-err: Jump only to the first live validation error from this extension. Compiler diagnostics are ignored for automatic navigation.
config.compileRevealTarget.enum.compiler: Jump only to the first compiler error reported by amxxpc. Useful if you want navigation to follow the real compiler result even when live validation is enabled.
Jump only to the first compiler warning. Useful when live validation already covers errors and you mainly care about warning cleanup after compile.
config.compileRevealTarget.enum.live-the: Prefer the first live validation error. If there is no live validation error, jump to the first compiler error instead.
config.compileRevealTarget.enum.all-issu: Recommended default. Prefer the first live validation error, otherwise the first compiler error, and otherwise the first compiler warning.
config.compileStartToastMode.markdownDes: Control whether a toast should appear right when compilation starts. This is only about the initial feedback toast before any compiler result exists.
config.compileStartToastMode.enum.never: Never show a toast when compilation starts. Recommended if you prefer less UI noise and rely on the progress indicator instead.
config.compileStartToastMode.enum.always: Always show a toast when compilation starts, before the compile result is known.
config.compileResultToastMode.markdownDe: Control which compile results should show a toast after compilation finishes. This is separate from both output channel reveal behavior and editor navigation to the first issue. The recommended `issues` mode shows toasts only for warnings or errors.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.never: Never show a result toast after compilation finishes.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.succe: Show a toast only for fully successful compiles with no warnings and no errors.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.warni: Show a toast only when compilation finishes with warnings and no errors.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.error: Show a toast only when compilation finishes with at least one error.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.issue: Recommended default. Show a toast when compilation finishes with warnings or errors, but stay quiet for fully clean success.
config.compileResultToastMode.enum.succe: Show a toast for every meaningful compile result: clean success, warnings, or errors.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.markdown: Control when the compiler output channel should be revealed automatically after a compile finishes. This decision is based on the real compiler result, not only on which diagnostics are currently published into the editor. The `issues` mode reveals output for warnings and errors and is the recommended default.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.enum.nev: Never reveal the compiler output channel automatically. Open it manually only when you want to inspect the full compiler log.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.enum.war: Reveal the compiler output channel only when the compiler reports at least one warning. Useful when live validation already covers errors, but you still want to catch compiler-only warnings immediately.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.enum.err: Reveal the compiler output channel only when the compiler reports at least one error. Keeps warnings quieter while still surfacing failed compiles.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.enum.iss: Reveal the compiler output channel when the compiler reports warnings or errors. Recommended default and the closest match to the previous boolean setting behavior.
config.compilerOutputRevealMode.enum.alw: Always reveal the compiler output channel after every compile, including fully successful compiles with no warnings.
config.documentContextCacheFileLimit.mar: How many recently used AMXX Pawn files keep their parsed hover, completion, and navigation context cached in memory. Use `0` for no limit. If you often keep many files open, setting a limit can reduce RAM usage. Older files are simply evicted from the cache and will be cached again automatically as soon as you return to them.
config.includeDocumentWarmupFileLimit.ma: How many include files the extension may quietly pre-open in the background for the active AMXX Pawn document to make the first Go to Definition into includes feel faster. Use `0` to disable this extra warmup, `-1` to warm every discovered include for the current file, or a positive number to limit how many include files are warmed. This does not affect hover, completion, include parsing, or original declaration lookup logic. It only pre-warms VS Code document models for navigation, so it can speed up both hover tooltip links and normal VS Code navigation such as F12 or Ctrl+Click. Higher values can use more RAM when many include files are involved.
config.persistentIncludeDeclarationCache: Disk budget, in MB, for this extension's persistent cache in VS Code global storage. Set to `0` to disable it and remove this extension's `.json` cache files. When enabled, the cache stores compact include declaration/preprocessor snapshots and full live-validation results, including clean `0 errors` results. Reopening VS Code or opening the same project again can skip most include parsing and, when the script text, settings, and include dependency stamps still match, restore full diagnostics immediately. Open editor documents and changed include dependencies are always rechecked before cached data is used; old entries are pruned automatically inside the extension-owned cache folder.
config.liveValidationMode.markdownDescri: Control continuous live validation for AMXX Pawn code without waiting for hover. This uses the same validation logic as hover where possible, but tries to stay CPU-friendly. The separate open/startup scan setting can still run one full pass even when this mode is `off`.
config.liveValidationMode.enum.off: Disable continuous live validation after edits and saves. A separate one-time open or startup scan can still run if enabled below.
config.liveValidationMode.enum.edited: Run one full scan on open or startup when that setting is enabled, then revalidate only the area you are actively editing.
config.liveValidationMode.enum.full: Run one full scan on open or startup when that setting is enabled, and always validate the whole file again after every change. Most complete, but also the heaviest mode.
config.liveValidationScanOnOpen.markdown: Run one full live validation pass when an AMXX Pawn file is opened, becomes the active editor, or is already active when the extension starts, regardless of the continuous live validation mode above. Disable this if you want faster editor opening and fewer startup CPU spikes. Document-context and include warmup still run in the background, so later hover, navigation, and the next edited or full validation pass can still benefit from warm caches.
config.liveValidationTypingDelayMs.markd: Delay, in milliseconds, before live validation runs after typing. Higher values reduce temporary diagnostics while a symbol or expression is still being typed. Set to `0` to validate only after the edit crosses a line boundary or the cursor leaves the edited line. Save/open validation still uses its own shorter timing.
config.liveValidationIssueMode.markdownD: Choose which live validation diagnostics should be scanned and published in the editor. `Errors only` skips warning-only passes where possible and keeps warnings out of Problems and live caches. `All together` also shows warning-level diagnostics such as self-assignment, unreachable code, redundant constant tests, and index-tag mismatch.
config.liveValidationIssueMode.enum.erro: Scan and publish only error diagnostics. Warning-only passes are skipped where possible, and warnings are filtered before editor diagnostics and cache writes.
Scan and publish both errors and warning-level live validation diagnostics. This is the most compiler-like and complete mode.
config.unusedStockValidationMode.markdow: Control whether live validation should analyze `stock` functions that are not currently reachable from real code. This only affects live validation noise and cost; navigation and other semantic features still know about those functions.
config.unusedStockValidationMode.enum.sk: Do not validate any `stock` function bodies or headers. Lowest noise and lowest cost for projects that use `stock` as helper libraries or templates.
config.unusedStockValidationMode.enum.re: Recommended default. Validate only `stock` functions that are reachable from non-`stock` code or from other reachable `stock` functions.
config.unusedStockValidationMode.enum.al: Validate every `stock` function, even if it is currently unused. Most complete, but can create more noise and extra work in large projects.
config.callbackSignatureMode.markdownDes: Control how strictly live validation should compare local `public` callback signatures against matching `forward` declarations from includes or local prototypes, and how it treats unused parameters on forward-backed callbacks. This only affects forward-driven callback checks, not ordinary duplicate/prototype validation.
config.callbackSignatureMode.enum.strict: Recommended default. Keep strict signature checks against matching forward declarations, including missing trailing parameters.
config.callbackSignatureMode.enum.compil: Be looser for `public` callback signatures and skip forward-driven parameter count/type mismatch checks, plus unused-argument warnings for forward-backed callback parameters. Useful when you want behavior closer to tolerant compiler callback patterns.
config.includeValidationMode.markdownDes: Control how aggressively standalone include files should receive live validation. Context-dependent include logic is still intentionally conservative even in strict mode.
config.includeValidationMode.enum.balanc: Recommended default. Keep current include-specific suppressions for checks that are often noisy without full call-site context.
config.includeValidationMode.enum.strict: Also run unknown symbol and invalid function call checks inside standalone include files. More complete, but more likely to surface context-dependent noise.
config.externalIncludeWatchMode.markdown: Control which include roots outside the current workspace should receive file-system watchers for dependency freshness and cache invalidation.
config.externalIncludeWatchMode.enum.wor: Watch only files inside the current VS Code workspace. Lowest watcher footprint, but external include edits may refresh only after reopening or recompiling.
Watch the workspace and configured global include roots. Good balance when most external includes come from your shared AMXX include folders.
config.externalIncludeWatchMode.enum.tra: Recommended default. Watch the workspace, configured global include roots, and already resolved external include targets from opened Pawn documents. Most reliable, with the highest watcher footprint.
config.debugOutput.markdownDescription: Write internal debug messages for live validation, lifecycle, watcher, and completion into the AMXX Pawn All-In Live Validation output channel. Disabled by default.
config.completionEnabled.markdownDescrip: Enable this extension's semantic AMXX Pawn autocomplete. Disable it if you want no completion items from the extension; when disabled, completion requests return immediately and do not build Pawn document context.
config.completionForwardDeclarationStyle: Choose how autocomplete expands `forward` suggestions when the cursor is at a top-level function declaration position. The same brace placement is also used for statement keyword snippets such as `if`, `else`, `for`, `while`, `switch`, `case`, and `default`, plus Enter-assisted bodies for manually typed function declarations; normal function-call completion still inserts a call snippet.
Do not add a function body for forward suggestions. Insert the same call-style snippet as ordinary functions.
Recommended default. Expand forward and statement snippets as `header { ... }` with braces on the same line.
Expand forward and statement snippets as `header` followed by braces on the next line.
config.completionCallArgumentMode.markdo: Choose how function-call autocomplete fills argument placeholders. This affects call usage only; forward implementation/declaration snippets keep their full signature.
config.completionCallArgumentMode.enum.r: Recommended default. Insert only required arguments before the first parameter that has a default value.
config.completionCallArgumentMode.enum.a: Insert placeholders for all declared arguments, including arguments that have default values.
config.completionAutoHideDelayMs.markdow: Automatically hide the completion widget after this many milliseconds without another completion request. Use `0` to keep VS Code's normal behavior. Empty results and a single suggestion that is already fully typed are hidden automatically regardless of this setting.
config.hoverMode.markdownDescription: Control how the extension's own semantic hover content should participate in normal mouse hover. This setting only affects AMXX Pawn hover content produced by this extension. It does not replace VS Code's built-in hover delay settings, and it does not change the separate persistent hover feature below.
config.hoverMode.enum.disabled: Do not provide the extension's semantic hover content during normal hover. Built-in VS Code hover behavior, such as diagnostics from the Problems system, can still appear.
config.hoverMode.enum.normal: Recommended default. Provide the extension's semantic hover content normally. The actual auto-show delay still depends on VS Code hover settings such as Editor > Hover: Delay.
config.hoverMode.enum.ctrl-hack: Ctrl only (experimental). Windows-only mode that tries to provide the extension's semantic hover content only while Ctrl is currently held during hover. This can be less stable than normal mode and may behave differently outside regular mouse hover. On non-Windows platforms it falls back to normal mode.
config.hoverMode.enum.shift-hack: Shift only (experimental). Windows-only mode that tries to provide the extension's semantic hover content only while Shift is currently held during hover. This can be less stable than normal mode and may behave differently outside regular mouse hover. On non-Windows platforms it falls back to normal mode.
config.hoverMode.enum.alt-hack: Alt only (experimental). Windows-only mode that tries to provide the extension's semantic hover content only while Alt is currently held during hover. This can be less stable than normal mode and may behave differently outside regular mouse hover. On non-Windows platforms it falls back to normal mode.
config.hoverContentMode.markdownDescript: Control how much information the extension should render inside semantic hover tooltips after hover is already allowed to appear.
config.hoverContentMode.enum.full: Recommended default. Show the full hover stack, including linked declarations, enum or struct member sections and extra descriptions when relevant.
config.hoverContentMode.enum.compact: Show the main semantic sections but reduce extra descriptions and secondary detail blocks. Useful when you want less tooltip noise without losing core context.
config.hoverContentMode.enum.signature-o: Focus on the main declaration or signature and suppress most extra detail sections. Useful when you mainly want a quick type or signature glance.
config.persistentHoverMode.markdownDescr: Control how aggressively the separate persistent hover feature should keep reopening the built-in VS Code hover at supported cursor positions. This does not change which positions are eligible for persistent hover. It only changes when that persistent reopen behavior is allowed to kick in.
config.persistentHoverMode.enum.disabled: Disable the persistent hover feature completely and leave only the normal transient hover behavior.
config.persistentHoverMode.enum.normal: Recommended default. Reopen persistent hover normally on supported positions such as function calls and include-mapped declarations.
config.persistentHoverMode.enum.error-co: Reopen persistent hover only when the currently edited context already has a live validation error nearby, such as on the same line or inside the current function. Existing persistent hover target rules still apply; this mode only adds an error-aware gate to reduce noise.
config.hoverGoToDefinitionLinksEnabled.d: Show clickable Go to definition links inside hover tooltips. This only affects tooltip links and does not change normal F12 or Ctrl+Click navigation behavior.
config.showThemeRecommendation.descripti: Show a recommendation to switch to one of the bundled AmxxPawnAllIn themes when editing AMXX Pawn files. These themes are tuned for the extension's custom Pawn token scopes, function signature hovers, and current or invalid argument highlighting.
